_note: Baseline INHERENT-EXPOSURE starting points by sector, as a scaffold for the assessor. Grounded in the risk framing of NIST SP 800-82, the NIST CSF, and the consequence-driven approach of IEC 62443-3-2, plus practitioner judgement. These are starting points the assessor confirms or overrides, NOT determinations. Geopolitical/threat modifiers are applied on top by the assessor.

sectors.name: Water / wastewater
sectors.note: Essential service, safety-relevant (treatment chemistry), increasingly targeted; consequence can be public-health.

sectors.name: Electricity transmission / distribution
sectors.note: CNI, credible state-level targeting (Industroyer, etc.), systemic and safety consequence.

sectors.name: Oil & gas
sectors.note: CNI, safety-critical (process safety), high-value target incl. state actors.

sectors.name: Nuclear
sectors.note: Safety-critical to the highest degree, heavy regulation, credible advanced targeting.

sectors.name: Discrete manufacturing
sectors.note: Consequence mainly operational/financial; targeted risk varies with product and IP; ransomware-exposed.

sectors.name: Process manufacturing (chemicals, etc.)
sectors.note: Process-safety consequence raises this above discrete manufacturing.

sectors.name: Food & beverage
sectors.note: Consequence mainly operational and supply-continuity; some safety; heavily ransomware-targeted.

sectors.name: Rail
sectors.note: Essential service, safety-relevant, regulated (NIS/CAF); consequence operational and safety.

sectors.name: Aviation
sectors.note: Safety-critical, regulated (CAA/CAF for Aviation), targeted interest.

sectors.name: Maritime / ports
sectors.note: Essential service, economic-systemic consequence, growing targeted interest.

sectors.name: Pharmaceutical manufacturing
sectors.note: Process safety plus high-value IP; targeted and ransomware-exposed.

sectors.name: Data centre / digital infrastructure
sectors.note: Systemic dependency for many others; NIS2 in scope; high availability consequence.

sectors.name: Building management / smart building
sectors.note: Consequence usually operational/comfort; can rise where life-safety systems integrated.

sectors.name: Other / not listed
sectors.note: Neutral starting point; assessor sets from criticality and consequence.

exposureModifiers.label: Operates in or serves a geopolitically exposed region or contested sector
Compromise has direct safety-of-life or major environmental consequence
Designated CNI / essential service / NIS2 essential entity
Many others depend on this organisation (single point of systemic failure)
Highly interconnected / large external attack surface
Compromise consequence genuinely contained and non-safety

hardRules: Baselines and modifiers scaffold the assessor's judgement; the assessor sets and can override the final exposure band.
Geopolitical judgements are the assessor's to make and record; the tool prompts but never asserts a geopolitical position on its own.
Safety-of-life consequence should not sit below 'high' without an explicit, recorded justification.
